findings.evidence: KeePass must be downloaded and installed
findings.rationale: Omits the target platform/operating system, version, distribution source, actor responsible for installation, and the precondition scope (which features or actions require installation).

findings.evidence: has no limits in length. A whole sentence can be used with more than 100 characters.
findings.rationale: 'No limits in length' is ambiguous as to whether a minimum length is also absent (allowing an empty password), and the illustrative phrase 'A whole sentence can be used' leaves unclear which characters (e.g., spaces, punctuation, Unicode) are permitted.

findings.evidence: Master Password has no limits in length
findings.rationale: Does not specify a minimum password length, any practical/testable upper bound, or the supported character set and encoding.

findings.evidence: Folder selected must be of type the database can read and that is “name”.kdb
findings.rationale: Poorly structured phrasing conflates a 'Folder' (directory) with a '.kdb' file, states that 'the database can read' the file rather than the application reading the database file, and does not clarify whether '“name”' is an arbitrary filename placeholder or whether '.kdb' is case-sensitive.

findings.evidence: Folder selected must be of type the database can read and that is “name”.kdb
findings.rationale: Does not specify the system's behavior if a user selects a file or folder that is not a valid readable '.kdb' file (e.g., filtering the selection dialog, rejecting the file, or displaying an error message).

findings.evidence: the previews one will be replace if selected
findings.rationale: Contains typos ('previews' for 'previous', 'replace' for 'replaced') and unclear referents: it is ambiguous whether 'the previews one' means a previously created database in the same directory or anywhere, and whether 'if selected' refers to choosing the same name, selecting the existing file, or confirming an overwrite prompt.

findings.evidence: Databases must have different names or else the previews one will be replace if selected
findings.rationale: Does not specify the scope of name uniqueness (same directory vs. global, case sensitivity) or whether the system warns the user and requests confirmation before overwriting an existing database.

findings.evidence: There must be entries in the database in order for them to be printed
findings.rationale: Does not specify what happens if the user attempts to print when the database contains no entries (e.g., disabling the print option or showing an error/warning message), nor whether printing applies to all entries or selected entries/groups.

findings.evidence: All data related to the word must be shown.
findings.rationale: 'All data related to the word' is vague: it does not define what 'related to' means (substring, exact, or case-insensitive matching), whether 'All data' includes displaying sensitive fields such as passwords in plaintext or only listing matching entries, and refers to 'the word' without an antecedent while the example uses a substring ('abc').

findings.evidence: All data related to the word must be shown.
findings.rationale: Does not specify which entry fields are searched, whether matching is case-sensitive, how matching data (especially passwords) is formatted or masked, or what happens when no matching entries are found.

findings.evidence: A name is required in order for the new group/subgroup to be created
findings.rationale: Does not specify what the system does if the user tries to create a group or subgroup with an empty or whitespace-only name, nor any naming constraints (maximum length, allowed characters, or uniqueness).

findings.evidence: A subgroup cannot be created when no group is selected
findings.rationale: Does not specify how the system enforces this restriction when no group is selected (e.g., disabling the subgroup creation control or displaying an error message).

findings.evidence: A name is required in order for the group/subgroup to be renamed
findings.rationale: Does not specify what happens when a user attempts to rename a group or subgroup with an empty or whitespace-only name (e.g., rejecting the change, reverting to the previous name, or showing an error), nor valid naming rules.

findings.evidence: In order to find something in a group a word must be placed in the find field
findings.rationale: 'something' does not specify what items or entry fields are searched, and 'a word' is ambiguous as to whether a whole word is required or any character, substring, or multi-word query is accepted.

findings.evidence: a word must be placed in the find field
findings.rationale: Does not specify what happens if a user triggers a search with an empty find field, how search results are displayed, or whether subgroups are included in the search.

findings.evidence: An entry must belong to a group to be created
findings.rationale: Awkward phrasing is ambiguous as to whether a group must already be selected prior to creating an entry (as in KP-008) or whether the user can select or assign a group during the creation flow.

findings.evidence: An entry must belong to a group to be created
findings.rationale: Does not specify how the system behaves if a user attempts to create an entry when no group exists or no group is selected (e.g., disabling entry creation, prompting to select a group, or assigning a default group).

findings.evidence: When the password field is completed the repeat password field must be completed
findings.rationale: 'the password field' and 'the repeat password field' lack an explicit antecedent/context, leaving unclear whether this applies to entry passwords, master passwords, or both; 'completed' is also vague as to whether empty/whitespace values count.

findings.evidence: When the password field is completed the repeat password field must be completed
findings.rationale: Does not specify the system's response if the password field is filled in while the repeat password field is left blank (e.g., preventing save or displaying a validation error).

findings.evidence: Password field and repeat password field must be identical
findings.rationale: Does not specify which screen or entity ('Password field and repeat password field') this applies to—entry creation/editing, master password setup, or both.

findings.evidence: Password field and repeat password field must be identical
findings.rationale: Does not specify how the system responds when the password field and repeat password field do not match (e.g., blocking submission, highlighting the fields, or displaying an error message).

findings.evidence: An entry must be selected to be viewed or modified
findings.rationale: Does not specify the system's behavior when no entry is selected and the user attempts to view or modify an entry (e.g., disabling the view/modify commands or showing an error message).

findings.evidence: When the password field is changed the repeat password field must be Changed and be identical with password field
findings.rationale: Does not explicitly identify whether 'the password field' refers to an entry's password field, the master password field, or both.

findings.evidence: When the password field is changed the repeat password field must be Changed and be identical with password field
findings.rationale: Does not specify what happens if the password field is changed while the repeat password field is not updated or does not match (e.g., blocking save or displaying an error message).

findings.evidence: When the password field is changed the repeat password field must be Changed and be identical with password field
findings.rationale: Duplicates the paired repeat-password requirement from KP-012 and the unconditional password equality rule already stated in KP-013.

findings.evidence: An entry must be selected before it is duplicated
findings.rationale: Does not specify what happens if duplication is attempted with no entry selected (e.g., disabling the action or showing a message), nor specify what duplicating an entry copies or alters (e.g., title suffix, target group, metadata).

findings.evidence: download new language translations For the following features, use cases are not included
findings.rationale: Missing sentence boundary merges a requirement with an editorial note, and 'the following features' has an ambiguous scope as to which subsequent requirements lack use cases.

findings.evidence: For the following features, use cases are not included
findings.rationale: Explicitly indicates that use-case specifications are omitted for subsequent features; also omits the download source/URL, installation steps for language translations, and error handling when no internet connection or browser is available.

findings.evidence: The prefix “Auto-Type:” is required in front of each sequence
findings.rationale: 'each sequence' refers to an undefined concept with no prior antecedent (not explaining what an Auto-Type sequence is or where it appears) and does not clarify whether 'Auto-Type:' is case-sensitive or requires a trailing space.

findings.evidence: The prefix “Auto-Type:” is required in front of each sequence
findings.rationale: Does not specify where sequences are entered (e.g., in an entry's notes field), the valid syntax of a sequence, or what the system does if the prefix is missing or malformed.

findings.evidence: Sequence’s length must not be more than a line (59 characters)
findings.rationale: Ambiguous as to whether 'Sequence’s length' includes the 'Auto-Type:' prefix and spaces, and conflates a layout-dependent 'line' with a fixed 59-character limit.

findings.evidence: Sequence’s length must not be more than a line (59 characters)
findings.rationale: Does not specify what happens if a sequence exceeds 59 characters or spans multiple lines (e.g., truncating, ignoring the sequence, preventing input, or displaying an error).

findings.evidence: If two auto-types are referred in one note field, only the first is used
findings.rationale: 'referred' is vague as to whether it means two 'Auto-Type:' declarations in the note field or references to auto-type definitions, and 'first' does not specify ordering (e.g., top-to-bottom appearance).

findings.evidence: If two auto-types are referred in one note field, only the first is used
findings.rationale: Only specifies the case of exactly two auto-types, omitting the behavior when more than two auto-types appear in a single note field and whether the user is notified that subsequent ones are ignored.

findings.evidence: two auto-types
findings.rationale: Uses the term 'auto-types' to refer to the same construct called 'sequence' / 'Sequence' with the 'Auto-Type:' prefix in KP-018 and KP-019.

findings.evidence: Only one database file is allowed in command line options
findings.rationale: Does not specify what happens if multiple database files are passed via command line options (e.g., refusing to start with an error message/exit code, opening only the first, or opening the last), nor specify the command-line syntax.

findings.evidence: database file
findings.rationale: Refers to the database as a 'database file', whereas KP-003 inconsistently refers to the '.kdb' database file as a 'Folder'.

findings.evidence: In case a space is found in the path, it must be enclosed into quotes
findings.rationale: The pronoun 'it' is referentially ambiguous—grammatically it could refer to 'a space' or 'the path'; additionally, 'the path' has no explicit antecedent (command-line database path vs. any path) and 'quotes' does not specify single vs. double quotes.

findings.evidence: it must be enclosed into quotes
findings.rationale: Passive voice leaves unspecified whether the user must quote paths when invoking command-line options or the system must automatically quote them; also omits the required quote character (single vs. double) and error handling for unquoted paths containing spaces.

findings.evidence: the database doesn’t open unless the password is entered
findings.rationale: States 'unless the password is entered' without explicitly specifying that the correct/matching master password must be entered.

findings.evidence: the database doesn’t open unless the password is entered
findings.rationale: Does not specify how the system responds when an incorrect password is entered or the input is left blank/cancelled (e.g., error message, retry prompt, or lockout behavior).

findings.evidence: the database doesn’t open unless the key file is present
findings.rationale: 'present' is vague: it does not specify where or how the key file must be located/provided (e.g., selected via UI, accessible on disk/removable media) nor that it must be the valid matching key file for that database.

findings.evidence: the database doesn’t open unless the key file is present
findings.rationale: Does not specify the system's response when the key file is missing, unreadable, corrupted, or does not match the database (e.g., showing an error message or prompting for a path).

findings.evidence: If there is a composite key
findings.rationale: 'composite key' is not defined in the document (e.g., how it is configured or whether other factors beyond master password and key file can be part of it).

findings.evidence: If there is a composite key, both master password and key file are required
findings.rationale: Does not state what operation requires both credentials (unlocking the database) or the system's failure behavior if either the master password or key file is missing or invalid.

findings.evidence: In case of lost master password or key file, the database never unlocks again.
findings.rationale: 'lost master password or key file' is ambiguous as to whether losing either credential prevents unlocking in all cases or only when that specific credential is required by the database's key configuration; 'never unlocks again' is also imprecise if the user later recovers a backup or recalls the password.

findings.evidence: In case of lost master password or key file, the database never unlocks again. There is no recovery
findings.rationale: Does not qualify that this applies specifically to the authentication credential(s) configured for the database (master password only, key file only, or either component of a composite key), nor specify any user-facing warning or feedback.

findings.evidence: File formats are not specialized password database formats
findings.rationale: 'File formats' is unqualified (unclear whether it refers to import/export formats, key files, or database files) and 'specialized password database formats' is vague and undefined.

findings.evidence: File formats are not specialized password database formats
findings.rationale: Does not identify which specific file formats (e.g., CSV, XML, TXT) or operations (e.g., import/export) are subject to this requirement.

findings.evidence: File formats are not specialized password database formats
findings.rationale: Directly contradicts KP-003, which requires a specialized KeePass password database file format ('“name”.kdb').

findings.evidence: File formats only specify a low-level layout of stored data
findings.rationale: 'File formats' is unqualified as to which formats are covered, and 'low-level layout of stored data' is vague and undefined.

findings.evidence: File formats only specify a low-level layout of stored data
findings.rationale: Does not specify which file formats or features this requirement applies to, nor define the concrete data layout or schema.

findings.evidence: Global hot key cannot be changed
findings.rationale: Does not specify what the fixed global hot key combination actually is, what action it triggers, or how conflicts with other applications using the same hot key are handled.

findings.evidence: Title, username or URL cannot be changed in a TAN entry.
findings.rationale: 'TAN' is an undefined acronym in the specification, and 'cannot be changed' is ambiguous as to whether these fields cannot be set even during entry creation or only cannot be modified afterward.

findings.evidence: Title, username or URL cannot be changed in a TAN entry.
findings.rationale: Does not define what a TAN entry is, what fixed or default values Title, username, and URL hold, or how the system enforces the restriction (e.g., read-only UI fields or error handling).

findings.evidence: When a TAN is used, it expires automatically and can never be used again.
findings.rationale: 'used' does not define which action counts as using a TAN (e.g., copying to clipboard, Auto-Typing, or viewing), and 'expires automatically' does not specify what expiration concretely does to the entry.

findings.evidence: it expires automatically and can never be used again.
findings.rationale: Does not specify how the system prevents reuse or responds when a user attempts to use an already-expired TAN (e.g., disabling copy/Auto-Type or displaying a warning/error message).
